title: AIRO Announces Jaunt–Vertiko Letter of Intent for Proposed Purchase of 10 JC250 Cargo Drones in Canada

body_markdown:
MONTREAL–(BUSINESS WIRE)– AIRO Group Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: AIRO), a next-generation aerospace and defense company, today announced that Jaunt, its wholly owned Canadian subsidiary, has entered into a non-binding letter of intent with Vertiko Mobilité for the proposed purchase of 10 JC250 drones and a strategic collaboration to develop autonomous cargo logistics operations in Canada using Jaunt’s JC250 vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) unmanned heavy-lift cargo drone.


The collaboration envisions an initial deployment of the 10 JC250 drones, which would represent an estimated value of $15–20 million, based on Jaunt’s current indicative pricing. These drones are intended to initially support logistics services for First Nations communities in Quebec and continued operational testing, with plans to subsequently integrate them into a broader logistics network developed from Mirabel.


An initial focus will be the Atikamekw community of Manawan, where Vertiko is working to establish an aerial logistics corridor connecting the community with the Joliette region. The initiative aims to improve access to essential goods, medical supplies, and other cargo in communities where conventional transportation can be costly, time-consuming, or constrained by geography and weather.


The JC250 combines vertical takeoff and landing capability with efficient forward flight, enabling cargo operations without the need for conventional runway infrastructure. Its capabilities are particularly well suited to connecting remote communities and supporting regional logistics networks.


“Partnering with Vertiko is an important step toward bringing the JC250 into commercial cargo operations,” said Dr. Simon Briceno, Chief Commercial Officer, Jaunt. “Our initial focus is on supporting First Nations communities with reliable, flexible logistics solutions while continuing to demonstrate the drone’s capabilities. We see significant opportunities to build on these initial operations and expand into regional cargo networks across Quebec and Ontario.”


Mirabel will serve as a strategic hub for the partnership’s future logistics operations. The existing facilities of the FBO Helibellule at Mirabel provide an established aviation infrastructure base for drone testing, operational development, and future cargo services. The location also benefits from its proximity to Jaunt’s drone development facilities and Greater Montreal’s aerospace industry.


Building on the initial First Nations applications, Jaunt and Vertiko intend to explore expanding JC250 cargo operations throughout the Greater Montreal region, connecting distribution points, businesses, and communities through more flexible cargo mobility services.


The longer-term vision includes supporting a proposed autonomous drone logistics corridor extending from Windsor, Ontario, to Montreal, Quebec. Such a network could connect major economic centers across the region, enabling drone-based cargo transportation between logistics hubs and supporting the development of more integrated regional supply chains.


“Through our collaboration with Jaunt, we are taking an important step toward establishing a new model for cargo transportation in Quebec,” said John Valley, President of Vertiko. “Our initial focus on the Atikamekw community of Manawan reflects our commitment to developing practical logistics solutions that improve connectivity and access to essential goods and services. By combining Jaunt’s JC250 drones with Vertiko’s operational expertise and existing aviation infrastructure in Mirabel, we see an opportunity to build a scalable drone logistics network that can ultimately serve communities and businesses across Quebec and beyond.”


The companies expect to continue refining operational requirements, conducting testing and demonstrations, and coordinating the activities necessary to support future commercial deployments. The letter of intent is not a firm order, requires no deposit, and either party may terminate it at any time. Any purchase of JC250 drones will occur only under a definitive purchase agreement, including final pricing of the JC250 drones, which remains subject to negotiation between the companies. These deployments also remain subject to drone readiness, applicable regulatory and internal approvals, and arrangements with relevant operators and stakeholders.


**About Jaunt**


Jaunt is a core business segment of AIRO, focused on the development of next-generation vertical takeoff and landing aircraft for defense and dual-use applications.


**About AIRO**


AIRO Group Holdings is a next-generation aerospace and defense platform driving innovation across defense and commercial markets. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, with operations in the U.S., Canada, and Denmark, AIRO combines a global reach with deep technical expertise.


Through an integrated model, AIRO delivers mission-critical solutions centered on its drone platforms, leveraging advanced avionics, integrated training capabilities, and embedded autonomy across systems.


**About Vertiko Mobilité**


Vertiko Mobilité is a Quebec-based company specializing in the development and operation of Advanced Air Mobility solutions. It deploys and operates drone-based aerial services, including Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS) operations, leveraging cutting-edge technologies and strategic partnerships. Through its operational expertise and ability to integrate emerging technologies, Vertiko Mobilité contributes to the development of an innovative aerospace ecosystem and the emergence of new aerial services across Quebec.
